whyChain.because: Customers contacted this queue more than the plan expected, so demand landed above forecast.

whyChain.why: Why did demand land above plan?
whyChain.because: Customer contacts did not disappear or appear — they arrived somewhere else. A related queue serving the same customers moved the opposite way at the same time.

whyChain.why: Why did contacts move between queues?
whyChain.because: Customers reaching this business can land in more than one queue. When routing or customer behaviour tips one way, one queue gains what the other loses while the total barely changes.

whyChain.why: Why did the forecast miss it?
whyChain.because: Each queue was planned on its own. The total across the related queues was closer to right than either queue individually, so the split between them is what failed.

whyChain.why: Why was the split between queues not anticipated?
whyChain.because: The evidence stops here. The cross-examination that could have confirmed the cause was interrupted before it could be validated, so we cannot say why the split was wrong.

executiveSummary: Demand came in above plan because contacts shifted from a related queue into this one.
The total volume across both queues was close to expected, but the split between them was not.
Each queue was planned separately, so the redistribution was missed.
The investigation could not be completed, so the exact reason for the shift remains unconfirmed.
